chunks: Certainly, what gathers people together (in categories) is (their) agreement and (their) disagreement,
for only one individual killed the camel of Thamud but Allah held all of them in punishment because all of them consented to it.
Thus, Allah, the Glorified, has said: “Then they hamstrung her, and turned (themselves) regretful.”
Then their land declined by sinking (into the earth) as the spike of a plough pierces unploughed weak land.

key_terms.الْخَسْفَة: Sinking or subsidence into the earth
key_terms.خُوَارَ السِّكَّة: The sound/impact of the plough spike
key_terms.عَمَّهُمُ: He encompassed them / held them all

ai.seo_question: How does a single person's action lead to the punishment of an entire community in Islamic theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the mechanism of collective accountability, noting that while the physical act may be performed by one individual, the community shares in the consequence through their collective consent (rida) or displeasure (sukht). He illustrates this with the story of Thamud, where the destruction of the camel by a single man resulted in universal punishment because the people unanimously agreed to it, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of communal actions. The narration further emphasizes the suddenness and totality of divine retribution, describing the earth swallowing them with a sound like a heated sword striking the ground.

en.sayed-ali-raza: certainly, what gathers people together (in categories) is (their) agreement (to good or bad) and (their) disagreement,
for only one individual killed the camel of Thamud [1] but Allah held all of them in punishment because all of them consented to it.
Thus, Allah, the Glorified. has said: “Then they hamstrung her, and turned (themselves) regretful.” (Qur’ān, 26:157).
Then their land declined by sinking (into the earth) as the spike of a plough pierces unploughed weak land.
